rationale: The two prior agreement runs used 12 percent loss. This successor runs the same five-node stress at 30 percent loss with a third seed (0x13198a2e03707344, run id 8), keeping the progressed-gated zero-divergence predicate and the fair-delivery convergence. The purpose is to exercise a materially harsher fault rate: a held comparison extends the scoped negative to that condition, while a violation would be reported with its first divergent index.

scope.description: Same five-node 900-action stress as seed 2, with seed 0x13198a2e03707344, run id 8 and a 30 percent drop rate, including the fair-delivery convergence phase and progressed flag.
assumptions: Only the seed and drop rate differ from the previously interpreted runs; harness logic and convergence are identical.
Messages may be delivered out of order or dropped; ticks drive elections and resends.
No snapshots, trimming or reconfiguration are used.
excluded: Snapshots, compaction, flexible quorums, reconfiguration, crash-restart and Byzantine participants.

experiment.prefix: Identical to the previous stress tests: build nodes 1..5, settle, then run 900 randomized actions (25 percent append, 20 percent tick, otherwise deliver or drop a random queued message with 30 percent probability), collect outgoing after each action, cap the queue, compare all decided prefixes, then run the fair-delivery convergence phase, compute progressed, and emit the safety event with run 8.

comparisons.description: Agreement under 30 percent loss: with progressed true, no two nodes may report different values at any index both have decided.
